title: What FEMA Pays Homeowners: FEMA homeowner aid against FEMA-recorded damage

topDisasters.title: Tropical Storm Bonnie and Hurricane Charley

faq.q: How much money does FEMA give homeowners after a disaster?
faq.a: Across 627 major disasters declared from 2002 to 2026, approved homeowner registrations received $3,619 on average from FEMA's Individuals and Households Program, counting home repair, rental and other-needs aid together. 47.6% of the 14,899,124 homeowner registrations were approved for any aid. Dollars are as approved, not adjusted for inflation.

faq.q: What is the maximum FEMA assistance for a homeowner?
faq.a: For disasters declared on or after October 1, 2026, FEMA's notice in the Federal Register sets the maximum at $46,400 for housing assistance and $46,400 for other needs; for disasters declared from October 1, 2025 it was $44,800 each. In FEMA's own data, 1.1% of approved homeowner registrations since 2002 received the maximum grant.

faq.q: Does FEMA pay for home repairs if I have homeowners insurance?
faq.a: Generally only for what insurance does not cover. FEMA's rules (44 CFR 206.113) let it help an insured homeowner when the claim is denied, when insurance proceeds are significantly delayed and the homeowner agrees to repay FEMA from them, or when insurance and all other help are not enough. Repair aid is limited to making the home safe and sanitary to live in (44 CFR 206.117), not to restoring it as it was.

faq.q: What share of FEMA applicants get approved?
faq.a: 47.6% of homeowner registrations in disasters declared from 2002 to 2026 were approved for any Individuals and Households Program aid. The share varies by disaster: 27% for Hurricane Irma in Florida, the largest by registrations, and 10% for the January 2025 California wildfires.

faq.q: Where can I download FEMA disaster aid data by county?
faq.a: This study publishes two CSV files under a CC BY 4.0 licence: every county with FEMA homeowner registrations since 2002, and every disaster by state, each with registrations, inspections, recorded damage, approvals and dollars. The underlying data is FEMA's OpenFEMA Housing Assistance Program Data (Owners) dataset, which is public and needs no key.
